canDo: Can accurately report other people’s views, questions and promises in past-tense indirect speech (sequence of tenses, converting time expressions, indirect questions), choosing reporting verbs that show the speaker’s attitude.
review: Review day 10’s past conditional (« le maire aurait déclaré que… » for unconfirmed information) and day 1’s layers of past tenses: in indirect speech, présent → imparfait, passé composé → plus-que-parfait, futur → conditionnel.
input: Read: a report on the limits of opinion polls, an editorial against “polls instead of debate” and a reader’s letter correcting a report (mark every reporting verb and the tenses being reported); listen: a radio report with interviews on a citizens’ assembly, a segment on vox pops and a local news flash (note “who said what, with which verb”).
output: Write: a formal letter (≥220 words) to the mayor on behalf of an association, accurately reporting what was said at a meeting to set the record straight; speak: a 3-minute monologue on the effect of publishing polls before an election, then a debate on “online public consultations”.
checkpoint: Reading and listening accuracy ≥80%; at least 5 instances of indirect speech in the letter, all with the correct sequence of tenses, and at least 4 different reporting verbs (affirmer, préciser, admettre, se demander si…); a 3-minute monologue without breaking off.
challenge: Today’s challenge: choose a news item on RFI’s « Journal en français facile » or TV5MONDE that includes a poll or a politician’s statement, and write 3 sentences of indirect speech (« Le ministre a affirmé que… », « Les journalistes se sont demandé si… »); then record a 1-minute spoken summary saying whether you trust the figures.

questions.why: The election is just the hook; the text discusses why polls get it wrong (abstention, question wording) and how readers should view them. A is the opening example; C: the text doesn’t describe the inner workings of polling firms.

« de nombreux sondés avaient affirmé qu’ils iraient voter, alors qu’ils étaient finalement restés chez eux ». B: the text doesn’t say the sample was too small; C is a general problem the sociologist raises, not Aubertin’s explanation of this error.

The same proposal, worded two ways, gave 70% versus 35%, and her conclusion is « un chiffre isolé n’avait aucune valeur tant qu’on ignorait la question exacte ». A and B treat the experiment’s results as genuine public opinion.
se défendre de qqch = to deny, to reject a claim; here, rejecting the idea of “throwing polls in the bin”. B twists it into a legal “defence”; C means the opposite.

« Il a toutefois admis que son institut devrait… publier systématiquement la marge d’erreur et le texte intégral des questions. » A is the opposite of « les grandes tendances étaient généralement bien mesurées »; C isn’t mentioned.
A “photograph” records the state of things at one moment; “not a prediction” means you can’t infer the result from it. B reads it literally; C is the opposite of the meaning.

« elles ont pris la place de l’argumentation », with the headline « Rendez-nous le débat ! ». A: the author says explicitly « Je ne conteste pas l’utilité des enquêtes d’opinion »; C: the school reform is just an example.

The guest wanted to explain the text first, but the presenter demanded a simple oui or non, « car le temps pressait ». A: the guest wasn’t refusing to take a position; B: the text doesn’t say the presenter didn’t understand the reform.
« Une opinion n’est pas un réflexe : elle se construit… elle évolue au contact des arguments adverses. » B is the opposite of the text; C over-extends it.
« Certains me répondront que les sondages permettent… C’est vrai. » is a concession. B: the text doesn’t defend the presenter; C is the mistaken idea the author criticises.
« pour chaque sondage publié, consacrons autant d’espace aux arguments de chaque camp ». Neither A nor C is proposed.
« Je me permets de rectifier cette affirmation… je vous demande de publier un rectificatif ». A: she isn’t against the project; B: she is only reporting the second meeting the mayor mentioned.
« 54 % d’entre eux approuvaient le projet, à condition que les places de stationnement soient conservées ». B is the newspaper’s version; C is the opposite of the condition.
« comme si leur avis représentait celui de tout le quartier ». A is the opposite — the article quoted the shopkeepers; C: she criticises the omission of figures, not their fabrication.
« Je ne prétends pas que le projet soit parfait. Mais… vos lecteurs ont le droit de savoir ce qui a réellement été dit. » A is the opposite of the text; B: the letter expresses no opposition.
« ils ont remis leurs propositions au maire », followed by a discussion of whether they will be implemented. Neither B nor C is covered.
« Il a déclaré qu’il avait lu toutes les propositions et qu’il en retiendrait au moins dix. » A exaggerates; C contradicts « il avait lu toutes les propositions ».
« au début, elle ne se sentait pas capable… elle avait beaucoup appris grâce aux experts invités ». A is the opposite of “thanks to the experts”; B isn’t mentioned.
« il attendrait de voir les décisions concrètes avant de se réjouir », and he asks what came of the last consultation — a cautious attitude. Neither B nor C fits.
« Le problème, c’est la suite… ils n’en ont gardé qu’une petite partie. » A: he says the deliberation stage is “often very successful”; C isn’t mentioned.
« il faudrait que les élus expliquent publiquement, proposition par proposition, ce qu’ils retiennent et pourquoi ils écartent le reste ». Neither A nor B is proposed.
« Un micro-trottoir, ce n’est pas un sondage… méfiez-vous. » A: free transport is just the topic of the vox pop; C: there is no national poll.
« elle m’a demandé qui paierait » — an indirect question with qui + conditional. Neither B nor C is mentioned.
« le présentateur a conclu que les habitants étaient massivement favorables… à partir de… six personnes ! » A: no contradiction is mentioned; C: no fabrication is mentioned.
« Ça donne de la couleur, de la vie, des voix. Mais ça ne dit rien de ce que pense l’ensemble de la population. » A is explicitly rejected; B isn’t mentioned.
« 61 % se sont prononcés en faveur du projet ». B is the opposite; C: the recording doesn’t say turnout was too low.
« les livraisons resteraient autorisées le matin, avant 10 heures ». A: work starts in the spring; C isn’t mentioned.
« si leurs clients venus en voiture continueront à fréquenter leurs boutiques ». A isn’t mentioned; B: they intend to ask for a meeting and haven’t been refused.

V12-01.zh: (at the time) the outcome seemed settled
V12-01.exZh: Three days before the vote, everyone thought the outcome was settled.

V12-02.exZh: With ten minutes to go, it all seemed settled, but the other team equalised.

V12-03.exZh: Social desirability bias leads respondents to present themselves better than they are.

V12-04.exZh: According to a poll published yesterday, residents remain divided.

V12-05.exZh: Two points separate the candidates, which is within the margin of error.

V12-06.exZh: Polling firms are accused of manipulating opinion, but they deny it.

V12-07.exZh: The newspaper published the full text of the questions put to respondents.

V12-08.exZh: The candidates won’t forget that election night any time soon.

V12-09.exZh: A simple percentage isn’t enough to close the debate.

V12-10.exZh: Opinions evolve through contact with other people’s arguments.

V12-11.exZh: A good debater takes the time to listen to the opposing arguments.

V12-12.exZh: That’s the price to pay for pluralism.

V12-13.exZh: I am writing to set the record straight.

V12-14.exZh: The daily agreed to publish a correction in its Monday edition.

V12-15.exZh: The minutes distorted her words, attributing hostile intentions to her.

V12-16.exZh: The citizens’ assembly brought together fifty citizens chosen by lot.

V12-17.exZh: The town hall organised a citizens’ assembly on the future of transport.

V12-18.exZh: Last night, the participants handed their proposals to the mayor.

V12-19.exZh: They felt they had been consulted only as a formality.

V12-20.exZh: The mayor promised a review in six months; we’ll see if he keeps his word.

V12-21.exZh: The radio station broadcast a vox pop recorded outside the station.

V12-22.exZh: The presenter claimed the population was overwhelmingly in favour of free travel.

V12-23.zh: to come out in favour of …
V12-23.exZh: 61% of participants came out in favour of the project.

V12-24.exZh: To be reliable, a survey must be based on a representative sample of the population.

V12-25.exZh: After twelve years in office, the outgoing mayor was beaten in the first round.

title: Reporting what others say
